text: dsh-neural-workflow 是面向 DSH Web 客户端的神经网络研究工作流插件。它注册 neural_flow 工具，以 Rust 中间件判定阶段与证据约束，并把会话日志投影为证据账本；还提供阶段图面板、工作流上下文、经验检索与逐阶段派发。适合需要按阶段推进研究并追踪证据的用户。无需 API 密钥；运行判定需要包内原生工作进程。

dsh-neural-workflow adds a research workflow to DSH web. Its neural_flow tool records evidence, Rust middleware checks stage constraints, and a panel shows progress and lessons. Researchers can plan one stage at a time. No API key is indicated; verdicts use the bundled native worker.
我想让神经网络研究按阶段推进，并知道下一步可以做什么。
有没有办法把研究证据记在会话里，并检查是否符合阶段要求？
Help me track research evidence and find relevant lessons while moving through a staged workflow.
dsh-neural-workflow 的功能「阶段证据记录与判定」：通过 neural_flow 工具查看状态或追加证据，Rust 中间件返回阶段判定和违规信息；证据账本从会话日志投影。
dsh-neural-workflow 的功能「工作流面板与逐阶段计划」：Web 面板显示工作流内容，工具可规划并派发单个阶段；执行器提供阶段数、时长和无进展预算。

[中文](README.zh.md) · **English**

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that puts the neural-network research workflow under **runtime constraint**: a stage graph, an evidence ledger folded from the session log, a lesson library of 611 recorded experiences, and a Rust middleware that blocks progress with no upstream evidence.

dsh-neural-workflow README · dsh-neural-workflow：Stages, gates and the lesson library come from this project's own skill (`skills/neural-paper-workflow/`), so what the graph enforces is what the workflow actually does — not an invented checklist.

dsh-neural-workflow README · 1. Stage graph with runtime verdicts：Ten stages across four layers, derived from the skill's 阶段编排:

```
L0 问题与设计   scope → develop
L1 执行         train → infer → validate
L2 证据与结论   conclude → write
L3 表达与交付   figure → polish → submit

Every node declares evidence kinds, a required-anchor flag, and a gate description taken from the skill's 质量门. The middleware computes, on demand:

dsh-neural-workflow README · 1. Stage graph with runtime verdicts：- `satisfied` / `ready` / `blocked` per node, with the blocking upstream nodes named
- per-layer completion
- the **frontier**: which stages may be worked on right now
- violations, each with its constraint code and a one-line diagnosis

dsh-neural-workflow README · 2. Six constraints (C1–C6)：| Code | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `C1` | **Reference integrity** — evidence may not point at a node the graph does not have. |
| `C2` | **Kind match** — a node only accepts the evidence kinds it declares. |
| `C3` | **Admission before advance** — evidence on a downstream node whose upstream is unsatisfied is out of order. |
| `C4` | **Traceability** — nodes that require anchors need `anchors[].path`. |
| `C5` | **Completion needs support** — a `completion` claim is refused while a mandatory node is still open. |
| `C6` | **Evidence completeness** — `kind` and `node` may not be empty. |
dsh-neural-workflow README · 2. Six constraints (C1–C6)：A constraint that cannot find its evidence stays silent: a criterion narrower than the facts would produce false positives.

dsh-neural-workflow README · 3. Evidence ledger：The ledger is not a database — it is a **projection of the session log**. The model records evidence with the `neural_flow` tool; the middleware validates it *before* it lands, and a rejected record comes back with the exact constraint that blocked it. Accepted evidence rides on the tool result, so it survives restart, resume, and compaction, and never pollutes the chat transcript with synthetic user messages.

dsh-neural-workflow README · 4. Lesson library (611 entries)：The whole `skills/neural-paper-workflow/knowledge/graph` is compiled into the plugin at build time:

| Kind | Count | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `idea` | 567 | Idea/experiment recipes: how to do ablation, calibration, leakage checks, figure work |
| `error` | 28 | Known errors with root cause, forbidden actions, and verification commands |
| `experiment` | 10 | Experiment design patterns |
| `perf`, `writing` | 6 | Performance and writing lessons |

dsh-neural-workflow README · 4. Lesson library (611 entries)：Two-step retrieval, matching how the skill's own engine works:

1. `neural_flow` with `action: "knowledge", query: "<symptom>"` → scored matches with a gist
2. `action: "knowledge", entry: "NP002"` → full entry (root cause, approach, command, forbid list)

Scoring is deliberate and explainable: title hits weigh 3, body hits 1, full-phrase-in-title +2, multiplied by severity (`critical` 3, `major` 2). Zero-score entries are dropped rather than returned as "maybe relevant" noise.

dsh-neural-workflow README · 5. Four UI surfaces：| Surface | Slot | What you get |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sidebar icon | `sidebar.panellist` (order 25) | Entry beside Plugins / Automation / Context Insights |
| Board page | `main` | Stage graph, layer bars, violations, ledger, lesson search |
| Session tab | `conversation.view` (order 25) | The same board bound to the current session |
| Right sidebar tab | `sidebar.right.pane.tab` + `.title` | The same board beside the chat, opened from the right Sidebar's guide card |

dsh-neural-workflow README · 5. Four UI surfaces：The right sidebar entry registers through the same public two-stage path dsh-context uses:
`ctx.sidebarRightTabs.register({ id, kind, title, guide })` declares the tab type, then
`sidebar.right.pane.tab` / `sidebar.right.pane.tab.title` supply its body and chip under that
same id. A harness without `sidebarRightTabs` skips the block entirely; the other three
surfaces are unaffected.

dsh-neural-workflow README · 5. Four UI surfaces：Styling uses only theme tokens (`--dsw-alias-*`), so light and dark both work. Layout is
**container-driven, not viewport-driven**: the right sidebar is ~300px wide inside a wide
window, so `@media (max-width)` never fires there. Breakpoints are `@container nwpanel`,
the graph measures its own container through `ResizeObserver`, and below 620px it switches
from one-layer-per-column to one-layer-per-row so node cards keep the full width instead of
collapsing into per-character CJK wrapping.
dsh-neural-workflow README · 6. Runtime context：A `systemPrompt` section states the current progress, the frontier, and any open violations — so the model knows what is ready next without being told.

dsh-neural-workflow README · 7. Experience ledger with a trust ladder：Lessons learned while working are stored per project under `$DSH_HOME/neural-workflow/projects/<key>/experience.ndjson` — append-only, never inside your repository.

| Standing | How it is reached | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `candidate` | a new record | visible, but never auto-recalled into the prompt |
| `derived` | 2 successful applications, or a human promote | auto-recalled for its stage |
| `canonical` | **only** `promote(id, 'canonical', { explicit: true })` | project truth |
section: 7. Experience ledger with a trust ladder

text: dsh-neural-workflow README · 7. Experience ledger with a trust ladder：A failed application demotes `derived` back to `candidate`; canonical only keeps the history. Contradictory records stay visible side by side and are never auto-merged. `recurrence()` clusters the same root cause across records.
section: 7. Experience ledger with a trust ladder

text: dsh-neural-workflow README · 8. Vocabulary, not bare strings：`lib/vocab.js` validates `node` and `kind` against the graph and returns the nearest candidates on a typo (`hypothesys` → `hypothesis`). It only ever *rejects more*, never accepts something the middleware would reject — the judgement stays in Rust.
dsh-neural-workflow README · 9. Failure admission：`kind: "failure"` records a failure that already happened. It is always admissible and never satisfies a node: failures are facts, not evidence.

dsh-neural-workflow README · 10. Dispatch plan：`action: "plan"` picks the next stage from the verdict, attaches the matching lessons and the real gate commands (`check_leakage.py`, `calibration_gate.py`, …) from the skill, and stops with a reason when the frontier is empty or the budget is spent.

dsh-neural-workflow README · 11. Contract baseline：`docs/schema-baseline.json` + `scripts/check-release.mjs` freeze the shapes others depend on — graph nodes/kinds, wire ops and error codes, evidence fields, accepted kinds — and fail the build when they drift.

dsh-neural-workflow README · 11c. Which lessons enter the request, and why：The stage brief carries lessons from a 613-entry library. Until now, selection was
BM25 top 6 plus a substring match, emitting `{id, title}` — no admission criterion,
no reason. Measured on the real library, that treated three very different kinds of
claim as equals:

| support | count | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cited | 102 | has external citations |
| sourced | 496 | traceable to a source event, no external citation |
| bare | 15 | assertion only |
section: 11c. Which lessons enter the request, and why

dsh-neural-workflow README · 11c. Which lessons enter the request, and why：Two library fields look like filters and are not: `status` is `formal` for all 613
entries, and `stage` puts 572 of them in `conception`. The `stage` tag is worse than
useless as a gate — reverse-checking by content, **172 of 182 entries that are
clearly about training are tagged `conception`** (validation 123/136, writing 21/24
likewise). It is an unpopulated default, so gating on it kills entries at random.

dsh-neural-workflow README · 11c. Which lessons enter the request, and why：So `lib/admission.js` decides admission by criterion, not by score, on two
independent axes:

- **role** — `hazard` 28 / `procedure` 35 / `guidance` 549 / `principle` 1. Role
  changes how a lesson enters: a hazard must be read first as a warning, a
  procedure as steps.
- **support** — how it is backed. Independent of role; a matched regex says the
  *problem* is detectable, not that the *advice* is true.

dsh-neural-workflow README · 11c. Which lessons enter the request, and why：Admission has exactly two channels: traceable support, or checkability
(`verification_cmd` — running it tells you if the advice holds). A bare assertion
enters only if its `prescan_pattern` actually matches the current evidence
ledger — formal confirmation, not similarity. Every candidate, admitted or not,
leaves `{reason, stageFit}`, and exclusion reasons are enumerable constants rather
than prose, so they can be counted and tested.

text:
dsh-neural-workflow README · 11c. Which lessons enter the request, and why：One narrow path is declared as narrow: of 593 entries carrying the
`prescan_pattern` key only **22 hold a non-empty pattern**, and 3 of those are
double-escaped data defects that compile but match a literal backslash. `19 usable
signatures, 3.1%`. The detection predicate must be *two consecutive backslashes* —
using "contains any backslash" flags every legitimate `\s` / `\.` / `\{` as broken.

dsh-neural-workflow README · 11c. Which lessons enter the request, and why：`plan` and `run` now share one `admitLessons` path, so the lessons in a plan and
the lessons at execution are the same set. The report rides back on the tool result
and is visible in the side panel.

dsh-neural-workflow README · 11b. Figure audit as a tool, not a judgement：`figure_audit` runs the project's five deterministic figure checkers — structure,
semantics, geometry, quality, rendering — and returns one merged report. It is a
separate tool from `neural_flow` because the input domain is different: one
operates on workflow state, the other on a file on disk.

Two failure modes had to be handled before this could be honest, both found by
running the checkers rather than reading them:
section: 11b. Figure audit as a tool, not a judgement

text:
dsh-neural-workflow README · 11b. Figure audit as a tool, not a judgement：| What the checker does | Why it lies | What the tool does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `check_figure_rendering` with no draw.io CLI returns `status=PASS, score=100`, every check `SKIP` | A pass that inspected nothing | Downgrades to `SKIPPED` with the missing dependency named; contributes no `PASS` row |
| `check_figure_geometry` / `check_figure_quality` exit 1 *when they find defects*, with valid JSON on stdout | Treating a non-zero exit as a crash deletes the very defects you need to see | Parses stdout first; the exit code becomes a per-check annotation, not the verdict |
section: 11b. Figure audit as a tool, not a judgement

text:
dsh-neural-workflow README · 11b. Figure audit as a tool, not a judgement：Formats are declared by what can actually be checked: `.drawio` gets all five,
`.pdf` gets geometry only (print-font floor), bitmaps and `.svg` get none because
every structural check needs the XML model. A missing checker directory is
reported as "no checks ran", never as "no problems found".
section: 11b. Figure audit as a tool, not a judgement

text:
dsh-neural-workflow README · 12. Read-only UI, tool-only operations：The panel **visualises**; it never mutates. There is no write route and no action
button: dispatch, evidence recording, feedback, promotion and claim linking all
go through the `neural_flow` tool, because they must pass the verdict, the budget
and the session identity — and all three live on the Agent side. The panel reads
the same verdict the tool produced, so it can never show a state that bypassed
the gate.

dsh-neural-workflow README · 12. Read-only UI, tool-only operations：This is clearAI's discipline kept intact: a UI write entry would be a second path
around the invariant, and a second path is how invariants die.

dsh-neural-workflow README · Architecture：```
graph/neural-paper-workflow.json   the stage graph (data — edit this, not the code)
native/                            Rust middleware: the ONLY constraint interpreter
lib/index.js                       host: projection, tool, prompt section, HTTP routes
lib/client.js                      browser: sidebar icon, page, session view, right-bar tab, lesson search

Three design rules are copied deliberately, and one thing is avoided.

dsh-neural-workflow README · Architecture：**From clearAI** — state has exactly one authority. `lib/fold.js` folds the session log; the projection, the tool, the panel and the prompt section all read that one fold. There is no second index to drift.

dsh-neural-workflow README · Architecture：**From dsh-ops** — the native worker is a managed subprocess with a line protocol, an explicit `selftest`, and an honest degraded mode. And the constraint judgement lives *only* in Rust: the host never re-implements it in JS, because a second interpreter is guaranteed to diverge. When the binary is missing the panel says so instead of silently substituting a different answer.

dsh-neural-workflow README · Architecture：**From Veyra** — knowledge is evidence-anchored and reused across sessions rather than re-derived. Here that shows up as `anchors[].path` on evidence, a ledger durable by construction, and a lesson library compiled from what earlier sessions already learned.

**Avoided** — no scoring heuristics pretending to be judgement. Every number the panel shows comes from either the Rust verdict or a deterministic fold.
dsh-neural-workflow README · Install：```sh
dsh-neural-workflow README · 1. build the lesson library from the skill (already committed, rerun when the skill changes)：node scripts/build-kb.mjs
section: 1. build the lesson library from the skill (already committed, rerun when the skill changes)

text: dsh-neural-workflow README · 2. build the native middleware (optional — the panel degrades to read-only without it)：bash native/build.sh
section: 2. build the native middleware (optional — the panel degrades to read-only without it)

text:
dsh-neural-workflow README · 3. install into a profile：dsh plugin --profile desktop add /absolute/path/to/dsh-neural-workflow
```

dsh-neural-workflow README · Verify：```sh
node scripts/build.mjs --check       # graph consistent, lib/graph-data.js current
node scripts/build-kb.mjs --check    # lesson index current with the skill
node scripts/check.mjs               # syntax, bundle shape, slot names, manifest
node scripts/render-check.mjs        # every registered component renders without throwing

`npm run check` runs the first five; `npm test` runs the last.

| `check_figure_rendering` with no draw.io CLI returns `status=PASS, score=100`, every check `SKIP` | A pass that inspected nothing | Downgrades to `SKIPPED` with the missing dependency named; contributes no `PASS` row |
| `check_figure_geometry` / `check_figure_quality` exit 1 *when they find defects*, with valid JSON on stdout | Treating a non-zero exit as a crash deletes the very defects you need to see | Parses stdout first; the exit code becomes a per-check annotation, not the verdict |

`.pdf` gets geometry only (print-font floor), bitmaps and `.svg` get none because
every structural check needs the XML model. A missing checker directory is

dsh-neural-workflow README · 12. Read-only UI, tool-only operations：The panel **visualises**; it never mutates. There is no write route and no action
button: dispatch, evidence recording, feedback, promotion and claim linking all
go through the `neural_flow` tool, because they must pass the verdict, the budget
and the session identity — and all three live on the Agent side. The panel reads
the same verdict the tool produced, so it can never show a state that bypassed
the gate.

dsh-neural-workflow README · 12. Read-only UI, tool-only operations：This is clearAI's discipline kept intact: a UI write entry would be a second path
around the invariant, and a second path is how invariants die.

dsh-neural-workflow README · Architecture：```
graph/neural-paper-workflow.json   the stage graph (data — edit this, not the code)
native/                            Rust middleware: the ONLY constraint interpreter
lib/index.js                       host: projection, tool, prompt section, HTTP routes
lib/client.js                      browser: sidebar icon, page, session view, right-bar tab, lesson search

Three design rules are copied deliberately, and one thing is avoided.

dsh-neural-workflow README · Architecture：**From clearAI** — state has exactly one authority. `lib/fold.js` folds the session log; the projection, the tool, the panel and the prompt section all read that one fold. There is no second index to drift.

dsh-neural-workflow README · Architecture：**From dsh-ops** — the native worker is a managed subprocess with a line protocol, an explicit `selftest`, and an honest degraded mode. And the constraint judgement lives *only* in Rust: the host never re-implements it in JS, because a second interpreter is guaranteed to diverge. When the binary is missing the panel says so instead of silently substituting a different answer.

dsh-neural-workflow README · Architecture：**From Veyra** — knowledge is evidence-anchored and reused across sessions rather than re-derived. Here that shows up as `anchors[].path` on evidence, a ledger durable by construction, and a lesson library compiled from what earlier sessions already learned.

**Avoided** — no scoring heuristics pretending to be judgement. Every number the panel shows comes from either the Rust verdict or a deterministic fold.
